question: A 40-year-old pregnant woman presents to the clinic at her 12th week of gestation. She does not have any complaints during this visit but comes to discuss her lab reports from her last visit. Her blood test results are within normal limits, but the abdominal ultrasound reports nuchal thickening with a septated cystic hygroma. Chorionic villus sampling is performed for a suspected chromosomal anomaly. Which of the following features can be expected to be present at the time of birth of this fetus?

options.opa: Congenital lymphedema of the hands and feet

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Nuchal thickening with a septated cystic hygroma" -> "Chorionic villus sampling performed" -> "Chromosomal anomaly suspected" -> "Possible chromosomal abnormality present at birth" -> 70% CHAIN: "Chorionic villus sampling performed" -> "Increased risk of genetic abnormalities" -> "Possible congenital anomalies at birth" -> 80% CHAIN: "Nuchal thickening with a septated cystic hygroma" -> "Increased risk of fetal anomalies" -> "Possible presence of congenital abnormalities at birth" -> 70%
analysis: The presence of nuchal thickening with a septated cystic hygroma on ultrasound is concerning for a chromosomal anomaly, specifically Turner syndrome. Turner syndrome is associated with lymphedema of the hands and feet (also known as webbed neck), which can be expected at birth.
